role.altitude: The orthoptist keeps confirming eligibility, explaining studies, measuring patients, writing the argument and presenting; searching records by hand, copying paper forms into study databases, answering avoidable data queries and merging mailed comments shrink.
skills_to_grow: Entering study data once with entry checks
Checking drafted text and citations against sources
role.ambitious_version: An orthoptist who can take part in more studies because the data handling no longer doubles.

tasks.short: List and confirm eligible patients, explain the study and obtain consent, perform study measurements, enter data, answer data queries, and attend meetings to participate in clinical research projects.

steps.what: Orthoptist lists clinic patients who may meet the inclusion criteria
Orthoptist confirms each patient's eligibility for the clinical research
Orthoptist explains the study and obtains informed consent
Orthoptist performs study measurements such as cover tests and prism measurements
Orthoptist records study measurements: on paper case report forms typed in later today, once on a tablet form in the study database after the change
Orthoptist checks the completed study form: measurements against the visit and the entry-check warnings, for the right study patient
Orthoptist submits the checked study form in the study database
Orthoptist answers data queries from the study monitor by mail

tasks.design: A saved query in the patient record lists the orthoptist's own clinic patients whose structured diagnosis, age and visit fields match the inclusion criteria, instead of a search through files by hand. The orthoptist confirms each patient. Measurements are entered once on a tablet form in the study database, with range and logic checks at entry, instead of paper forms typed in later; the orthoptist checks each form and submits it once. The checks catch most errors before the monitor raises a query. Consent, measuring and meetings stay with the orthoptist.

approvals.approved_version: The study form for this patient and visit exactly as checked by the orthoptist in s5c, submitted once in the study database; any correction needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Candidates were found by hand and data written twice.
tasks.enabler_now: Saved record queries and study forms with entry checks.
tasks.still_hard: Criteria that live only in free-text notes.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a study so a parent can decide for a child.

evidence.claim: Study forms with range and logic checks at entry catch errors before monitoring.
Health data are special category data; a DPIA is expected.

assumptions: Boundary: taking part in research; evaluating and treating disorders (task 18430) and interpreting test results (task 18431) are sibling tasks.
The record query runs only on the orthoptist's own clinic patients, and the ethics committee approved this way of recruiting.
s5 saves the second entry of paper case report forms.
Input contract for s6: the study sponsor sets up entry checks in the study database for about 60% of studies; s6 is priced at that share.
Consent, measuring, meetings and the form check and submission keep their full time. s5 keeps 50 because writing the measurements stays and only typing them in again goes.
research_questions: Do data queries per patient fall?

incremental.description: Orthoptist adapts the saved query for each new study.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: criteria are mostly free text, so the query finds few patients (s1 keeps 70), and few sponsors set entry checks (s6 keeps 85) (9.8); high: structured criteria and entry checks in 60% of studies (14.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review literature, analyse data, write the paper, merge co-author comments, format to journal style, approve and submit, prepare slides, and present or publish scientific papers.

steps.what: Orthoptist reviews literature for the scientific paper

loop.input: The research question and a literature database.
loop.output: Ranked papers with short summaries, each linked to its source.
loop.check: Every reference must resolve to a DOI. A second check flags summary sentences that cannot be found in the paper's abstract; the orthoptist opens every cited paper and checks the summary against it before use.
loop.stop: The orthoptist searches by hand when known key papers are missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Orthoptic studies use varied terms for the same conditions.

steps.what: Orthoptist analyses data and makes tables and figures
Orthoptist writes the paper or abstract

loop.input: The orthoptist's outline, the results tables and the checked reference list.
loop.output: Draft methods and results sections in the journal's structure.
loop.check: Every number must match the results tables and every citation must come from the reference list, or the draft stops. A second check compares each methods and results sentence with the tables and protocol and flags sentences they do not support; the orthoptist resolves every flag and edits the sections.
loop.stop: The orthoptist writes by hand after two failed checks; the introduction and discussion are always written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each study needs its own text.

steps.what: Orthoptist merges co-author comments from mailed copies
Orthoptist formats the manuscript and references to journal style
Orthoptist collects co-author approval of the final manuscript
Orthoptist checks the final manuscript and author list against the co-author approvals, and the journal or congress it goes to
Orthoptist submits the manuscript to the journal or congress
Orthoptist prepares slides to present the paper
Orthoptist presents at the congress and answers questions

approvals.approved_version: The manuscript file and author list exactly as approved by all co-authors and checked by the orthoptist in s6, submitted once to the journal or congress named there; any change needs new approval and a new check.

tasks.design: A literature search returns ranked papers with linked summaries, and the orthoptist opens every source. A saved analysis script makes the tables and figures. A drafting step writes the methods and results sections from the results tables and the checked reference list; the orthoptist writes the introduction and discussion and edits the rest. Co-authors comment in one shared document instead of mailed copies. A reference manager and the journal template handle formatting. Slides reuse the paper's figures. Approval, submission and presenting stay with the orthoptist, and use of AI is disclosed to the journal.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comments came back in separate mailed copies and formatting was done by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared documents, reference managers and drafting tied to a results table.
tasks.still_hard: Writing the discussion of an unexpected result.
tasks.human_edge: Framing a finding so ophthalmologists change practice.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting and merging; the argument stays.

evidence.claim: Literature, protocols and research work suit an artefact generator with citations.
Many journals require disclosure of AI use and do not accept AI as an author.

assumptions: Boundary: presenting or publishing papers; training students and health professionals (task 18440) and preparing reports for practitioners (task 18436) are sibling tasks.
s4 saves merging comments from several mailed copies into one file.
Only pseudonymised results tables go to the drafting step; no patient data.
Approval, submission and presenting keep their full time.
research_questions: Are papers submitted sooner after the study ends?

already_counted.description: Orthoptist edits drafted methods and results.

incremental.description: No new work: opening and checking every source is in the remaining time of s1 and s3, and the script and template are kept with the study.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short abstracts where search and drafting help little (s1 and s3 keep 90) and co-authors still mail comments (s4 keeps 80) (15.6); high: full papers with many co-authors in the shared document (23.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
